thread:
Nora: Quick catch before I lock the weekly KPI slides — launch_posts CPL looks unrealistically good but webinar signups and SFDC leads are down. anyone else seeing a mismatch?
Etta: yep saw it too. CTR steady, attribution-revenue up ~40%, raw portal rows down ~22%.
Sam: I pulled the dashboard query — looks like the attribution window changed on the dashboard view from last_click to 30d_data_driven overnight?
analytics-bot: config-check: "Postlaunch Overview" report had dimension 'attribution_model' toggled to data_driven at 2026-03-29T03:12:05Z by @marco (dashboard edit). Previous default was 'last_click'.
Luis: whoops, I toggled that while testing a bench narrative. That will reassign credit and inflate CPL appearance.
Nora: ok that's a big find. But why are portal rows down? could be unrelated UX or ingestion.
Sam: running a quick join to compare clicks -> form_submit for 03/28 12:00-14:00 UTC.
Sam: ```sql
SELECT date_trunc('minute', ts) as m, sum(case when event='click' then 1 else 0 end) clicks, sum(case when event='form_submit' then 1 else 0 end) submits
FROM events_raw
WHERE campaign='launch_posts' AND ts >= '2026-03-28 12:00:00' AND ts < '2026-03-28 14:00:00'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```
Sam: summary: clicks ~1,420; submits ~19 (baseline ~46).
Etta: submit drop is independent of attribution model flip. any infra notes?
ops-bot: consumer-lag: detected kafka consumer lag 12k between 12:07-12:18 UTC; service restart at 12:10 UTC. error-rate spike on form-handler 502 at 12:08.
Nora: so two things: 1) dashboard attribution model flip making performance look better; 2) actual submit/lead loss during 12:07-12:18 due to service lag. both must be in the deck.
Luis: for the benchmark narrative I'll revert the dashboard to last_click for the weekly deck and include an appendix with the data_driven view for transparency.
Etta: can analytics estimate how many leads are recoverable from backfill vs permanently lost?
analytics-bot: backfill-estimate: recoverable events: 20, unrecoverable: 7. queued backfill job id bf-1765987221. ETA ~30m.
Sam: note: we pushed messaging variant E at 11:50 UTC to a 15% audience. early stats show variant E conversion 0.9% vs control 2.4% in the prior 24h. if backfill doesn't recover, variant E looks like a regression.
Nora: action items: 1) Luis revert attribution model for the deck and add footnote calling the day an "attribution model + ingestion anomaly". 2) analytics to run backfill and mark reconciled leads provisional. 3) Sam to keep compatibility logs and check whether 422s or validation rejections correlate with the lost submits. 4) Legal signoff if analytics plans to synthesize leads from access logs.
Legal: quick note — any synthetic reconciliation must have an audit trail and be labeled "reconciled provisional" before external outreach.
analytics-bot: backfill completed: reconciled +18 events. net gap vs baseline now -5. provisional list posted to #analytics.
Luis: dashboard reverted to last_click. added appendix slide with data_driven model and a 1-line explanation.
Etta: pausing variant E to 0% audience while we investigate. posting rollback note to #launch-posts.
Sam: rollback posted and compatibility flag enabled on form-handler. logs show validation rejections at 12:08 were due to a rare payload shape from older clients; compatibility mode accepted them.
Nora: for the weekly KPI deck: main numbers = last_click adjusted baseline; include an "Anomaly" slide with: timeline (12:07-12:18 UTC), causes (consumer lag + variant E + dashboard attribution flip), remediation (backfill + rollback + dashboard revert), and next steps.
Etta: recommend we add an automated check: alert when dashboard_cohort_conversions differ from portal_count by >20% for 20m. I'll add to asks for eng-ops.
ops-bot: alert-rule drafted (id alert-1765987233). posting to #eng-ops for review.
Nora: thanks everyone. I'll finalize the deck with provisional reconciliation numbers and a visible footnote. will hold external webinar claims until Legal thumbs up. :white_check_mark:
